title: Zichron Menachem – Association for Children with Cancer and Their Families

trailer.text: Miri and Haim Arenthal, residents of Jerusalem, are the founders of the Zichron Menachem association and winners of the Israel Prize for Lifetime Achievement for the Hebrew year Tashat.
Their eldest son, Menachem, fell ill with cancer and fought the disease for 14 years, until he died in 1990.
Four months after his death, the couple founded Zichron Menachem, an Israeli association that helps children with cancer and their families.
According to the description of the winners at the Israel Prize ceremony, since its founding in 1990 the association has helped 47,753 sick children and their families.

paragraphs.text: Miri Ehrental was born and raised in Jerusalem.
She was the fourth daughter in a Haredi family of seven children.
According to ynet, Miri and Chaim married in 1973 and had six children.
The eldest of them was Menachem.
Menachem was diagnosed with cancer when he was a baby.
According to Israel Hayom, after a bone marrow test it was finally established that he had blood cancer.
According to Israel Hayom, over 14 years the disease was discovered, treated, went into remission and attacked again, five times.
When Menachem was 14, the disease returned for the fourth time, and the doctors recommended a bone marrow transplant.
It was an innovative procedure, and only 122 patients in Israel had undergone it at the time.
His brother Tzviki donated bone marrow to him.
Miri said that in those years people did not talk about cancer as they do today, and did not say the word explicitly.
The couple recalled that during the struggle there was no one to extend a hand to them.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Menachem died on April 8, 1990.
According to ynet, four months after their son's death the couple came up with an idea: a blood donation body for cancer patients.
Miri said that they decided to found an association so that other families could benefit from their experience.
According to Aish.com, a month after their conversation they decided to act, and three months later they held the association's first event.
According to the Jewish Chronicle, to fund the new organization they held a big concert with Avraham Fried and Mordechai Ben David.

In the association's early days, and in view of the difficulty the couple themselves had experienced in finding donors of blood components, the couple established a database of potential donors at Hadassah Ein Kerem.

stations.title: A home for children who cannot go to kindergarten

paragraphs.text: In the mornings, children whose immune systems do not allow them to go to kindergarten and school come to the association's building in Jerusalem.

Miri said at the Israel Prize ceremony that the association provides others with exactly what she and her husband had lacked: a warm home for sick children who cannot go to kindergarten and to schools.
According to Aish.com, the association brings hundreds of children each day by bus to the "House of Dreams", a center full of activities.
According to Kol-Zchut, the association runs a day center, a guest center for families, programs for catching up on studies, classes and workshops.
According to the Jerusalem Post, it also has support groups for parents.
For parents whose child has died, it offers guidance sessions once a month, for 12 months.
According to Kol-Zchut, the association runs a bone marrow donor registry and a registry of blood and platelet donors.
According to Aish.com, in 2011 the association launched its first nationwide hair donation campaign, so that every woman with cancer in Israel would have a wig.
According to Aish.com, Chaim Ehrental designed a portable hospital, the first of its kind, which accompanied the association across Europe.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the conditions for taking part in the programs are a child fighting cancer and an Israeli family.
The participants come from every background: religious and secular, Jews, Christians, Muslims and Druze.
According to the Israel Prize committee, the association has many projects that bring together different populations, without distinction of religion, race or sex.
In May 2019, about 100 parents and children traveled to London for a week, and the association paid all the expenses.

According to the Jerusalem Post, the El Al flight to London that the association organized for a week-long vacation carried 130 Israeli children fighting cancer and another 110 accompanying volunteers.
One of them was Sira, a 14-year-old Muslim Arab-Israeli girl with cancer.
Chaim Ehrental said in 2019 that at least 90% of the money the association raises comes from private individuals.
According to the Jerusalem Post, it is registered as a nonprofit organization in four countries and operates in at least six.

stations.title: Jerusalem Prize, beacon and Israel Prize

paragraphs.text: In 2015, when the association marked 25 years since its founding, Miri Ehrenthal and the organization 'Zichron Menachem' were chosen to receive a special Jerusalem Prize marking 25 years of kindness, awarded by the Jerusalem Conference of the newspaper 'Besheva' ‹c53›.
According to the prize citation, Zichron Menachem is the first organization in Israel to have supported this population on a national scale.
Education Minister Naftali Bennett informed the couple that they had won the Israel Prize for Lifetime Achievement for the Hebrew year Tashat.
Bennett said of them that they are the angels of giving of the people of Israel, and that out of loss they created an enterprise of kindness.
According to the Ministry of Education announcement, the organization is the first of its kind and among the most comprehensive established in Israel to give broad support to patients and families.
Chaim and Miri received the prize at Binyanei HaUma in Jerusalem, on Chaim's 69th birthday.
The couple said that with the prize grant, about 75 thousand shekels, they would renovate the house a little.

disagreements.question: How many children has the association helped?

versions.says: Description of the winners at the Israel Prize ceremony (2019): 47,753 sick children and their families
Jerusalem Post (August 2019): almost 36,000 children who fought cancer

disagreements.question: At what age was Menachem diagnosed with cancer?

versions.says: ynet: a year after he was born
The Jewish Chronicle and Aish.com: at two years old

disagreements.question: At what age did Menachem die?

versions.says: Jerusalem Post: at 15 and a half
Jerusalem Post, in another article: at 14

disagreements.question: When did Menachem say he did not want to keep fighting, and to whom?

versions.says: Aish.com: two weeks before his death he told his parents he did not want to keep fighting
Miri, in Israel Hayom: six days before his death he asked the doctor to stop the blood transfusions as well

disagreements.question: When did the couple request recognition from the Ministry of Education?

versions.says: Chaim Ehrental, in Israel Hayom: ten years ago
Chaim Ehrental, in ynet: "not long ago", which is why they expected to receive an institution code from the state

disagreements.question: What happened four months after Menachem's death: was the idea only raised, or had the association already been founded?

versions.says: ynet: four months after the death, the couple came up with the idea of setting up a blood donation body
Israel Hayom: on Tu B'Av, four months after the death, the association had already been founded
The Jewish Chronicle: four months after the death, the couple founded the association
